Flash Floods in 2016 Disrupted Jordan’s Oil and Gas Producers

AMMAN, June 11 – Severe flash floods that struck central Jordan in March 2016 led to significant disruptions for the country’s oil and gas producers, according to industry officials and analysts. The flooding, triggered by unusually heavy rainfall over a 48-hour period, inundated processing plants and damaged key transport routes, forcing several operators to temporarily halt production.

Among the hardest hit was Petra Energy Resources, which reported that floodwaters breached its Ajloun processing facility, causing a complete shutdown for five days. “The safety of our staff was our first priority,” said Fawaz Al-Qudah, the company’s operations manager. “We resumed operations only after extensive safety checks and repairs.”

Road closures along highways linking production sites to storage terminals further hampered logistics. The Jordanian Oil and Gas Producers Association estimated that combined output across affected sites fell by up to 30 percent during the week following the floods, with some companies experiencing delays in fulfilling delivery contracts.

Industry analyst Sami Haddad noted that the disruptions highlighted vulnerabilities in the sector’s infrastructure. “Many facilities were built with drought in mind, not sudden floods,” he said. “This event underscored the need for better flood defenses and contingency planning.”

No fatalities or major injuries among workers were reported, but union representatives called for improved emergency procedures. By late March 2016, operations had returned to normal, and subsequent investments in flood mitigation measures were announced by leading companies in the months following the incident.
